title: Overlapping networks with the same SSID are handled confusingly
line: When a saved Wi-Fi network rejects its password while connecting on its own, Plasma now shows a notification with an Enter Password button instead of popping up a password dialog.
explanation: When the saved password of a Wi-Fi network fails, NetworkManager asks the secret agent for a new one (RequestNew). plasma-nm's agent in kded answered every such request with a password dialog, so a background reconnect, such as roaming onto another access point with the same name and a different key or a hotspot restarting, suddenly put a modal dialog in front of the user. Now, when the request was not started by the user (no UserRequested flag) and the connection is Wi-Fi, kded shows a persistent "Could not connect to this network. The password may be wrong or may have changed." notification with an Enter Password… button that opens the same dialog. Closing the notification cancels the request like Cancel in the dialog; NetworkManager cancelling closes it; if NetworkManager has stopped waiting (its 2-minute agent timeout), the button connects again so NetworkManager asks for the password anew. Connections the user starts still show the dialog right away.

commits.message:
kded: use a notification for background Wi-Fi password failures

When a known Wi-Fi network rejected its password while connecting on its
own, for example because another access point had the same name, a
password dialog popped up. Show a notification with a button instead.

BUG: 420170

media.caption: Background wrong-password request for HomeWiFi (no UserRequested flag): a password dialog pops up over the user's work.
Same request with the fix: a notification with an Enter Password… button, no dialog.
